reason: Re-opened packet.js gita 9 --verse 9.26 (Govindacharya 1898, archive.org gita-bhasya): in Rāmānuja's own segment on 9.26 the Lord is 'He Who is all-satisfied' and 'naturally in the enjoyment of supreme felicity', yet enjoys the offering 'as if I came (anew) in possession ... of a treat so rare as to be beyond the most distant expectations of a desiring heart'. That carries every clause of the paraphrase (wanting nothing, ever in bliss, relishing as if newly given, beyond hope) with no drift; the page header '25-27.' is OCR running matter, not a joint segment, so the locator 9.26 stands. Nothing rests on Besant's 'striving self' (Telang/Śaṅkara 'pure-minded'). verse.js ok at Bhagavad Gita 9.26 [363]; the key is the natural line for this reading. Plain sense checked in day.js: 9.20 to 9.21 give the Soma-drinkers' heaven and return, 9.25 ends with 'My worshippers come unto Me', 9.26 turns to leaf, flower, fruit, water; no four-word run from the verse, no doctrine. School named, no comparison or other tradition (the Shining Ones are the text's own), tone neutral. entry-check.js ok with no warnings; 43 words, one semicolon, verb 'reads'.
